title: Convex-hull conjecture for Orthomin(1)
statement:
Let $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_d\in\mathbb{C}$ be the spectral points used in the finite-dimensional Orthomin analysis, and let $\operatorname{Hull}(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_d)$ denote their convex hull. Let $q_n$ be the Orthomin$(1)$ residual convergence factor and let $\rho$ be the parameter in the associated linear system. **Convex-hull conjecture.** If

$$
-\rho\in\operatorname{Hull}(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_d),
$$

then

$$
q_n\to\rho.
$$

The paper describes this as a sharpened version of its earlier conjecture. The preceding proposition proves only the complementary obstruction that $-\rho$ outside the convex hull implies $q_n$ does not converge to $\rho$; the stated implication is therefore left open in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.2669

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2011).
source_name: Andrei Draganescu and Florin Spinu, “Sharp estimates for the convergence rate of Orthomin(k) for a class of linear systems”, arXiv:1109.2669 (2025).
